ksp_mappings.explanation: Workflow productivity contributes directly to the highest-scoring office prompts through contracts, invoices, forms, project papers, and meeting packets. It is not forced into café, gaming, home, or creative alternatives when the scene would become unnatural.
Enterprise security is acknowledged as source context for managed office environments, but security policies are not made visible as special paperwork because that would over-specify the scene.

Fleet integration and lifecycle adaptability support the broad managed-office context in grounded prompts, but technical integration details are omitted from the visual prompts because they are not ordinary visible materials.
Sustainability is omitted from prompt text because environmental credentials are not a visible lifestyle setting cue at C-Tech's level of description.

value_proposition.explanation: Together, the sources position the product as a secure, fleet-ready monochrome office solution for managed enterprise teams moving business-critical documents. Prompt relevance is strongest where an ordinary corporate office surface holds contracts, invoices, forms, project papers, or meeting packets; non-office scenes are included for required diversity and marked as adjacent or creative departures.

debug.input_assessment: Both documents describe the same enterprise print product direction and align on managed fleets, shared workteams, business-critical black-and-white document output, contracts, invoices, forms, meeting packets, and project documentation. The smart brief adds audience detail such as IT, operations, finance, legal, HR, administration, and shared office hubs. Source messaging provides clean KSP structure and eTail-ready wording. Neither document provides lifestyle support for gaming, education, café, or creative studio settings; the smart brief explicitly warns against home, photo, or creative printing as primary use cases.
debug.count_explanation: Generated exactly 20 distinct prompts. The set covers Home, Office, Education, Gaming, Café, and Creative Studio, with source-grounded office scenes sorted first by source relevance and C-Tech-led alternatives retained later for diversity.
ignored_fields: Runtime metadata, run IDs, timestamps, status labels, and model names were treated as non-scene metadata.

Hardware specifications, security stack names, firmware details, connectivity details, certifications, SEO rankings, and competitive search data were not translated into visible props unless they described an ordinary setting or document material.
The target device identity and appearance were excluded from all prompt text.
debug.diversity_summary: The bank moves among corporate offices, integrated-shelving office tables, shared office hubs, creative offices, café tables, home workspaces, a living-room end table, classroom and library study surfaces, and gaming desks. Office prompts carry the source-specific document materials; at least six later prompts remain C-Tech-led alternatives without importing enterprise paperwork into unsupported settings.
limitations: The camera profile allows a medium oblique view with at most two local props and one background detail, so many C-Tech reference inventories were simplified.
No people were added, even where the profile allows partial activity, because the references do not require people and the source tasks can be expressed through ordinary materials.
Non-office categories are required for coverage but are weakly supported or unsupported by the source documents.
Technical product claims such as security, firmware upgradeability, speed, connectivity, and sustainability are not directly visible in these lifestyle environments.

Corporate and shared office contexts, including office hubs and document-heavy departments.

Security, fleet management, connectivity, speed, and sustainability details are mostly technical and not visible as ordinary scene props.
No direct support for café, gaming, classroom, library, or living-room environments.
